messages.author: e4c2f75e7fcb66ed
messages.subject: partial metric invariance
parts:
Hi,

I'm trying to study measurement invariance in a questionnaire of 6 items across 2 groups, postulating 2 underlying factors. The case has exactly the same formulation as the example in the following presentation:
http://www.lesahoffman.com/948/948_Lecture9_Invariance.pdf

I can successfully estimate the CONFIGURAL version of the model:
m.fa.config <- ('  
          EXT =~ X1 + X2 + X3
          INT =~ X4 + X5 + X6
        ')
fa.config <- cfa(m.fa.config, 
           data = items.sm2,  
           group = "cohort")

and also the METRIC INVARIANCE version of the model, where I free all the loadings and restrict the variances of the factors to 1 in the reference group:
m.fa.metric <- ('
                EXT =~ c(NA,NA)*X1 + X2 + X3
                INT =~ c(NA,NA)*X4 + X5 + X6
                EXT ~~ c(1,NA)*EXT
                INT ~~ c(1,NA)*INT
                ')
fa.metric <- cfa(m.fa.metric, 
                 data = items.sm2, 
                 group = "cohort",
                 group.equal = c("loadings")
                 )

I can then see that the metric invariance test is failed:
Chi Square Difference Test

          Df    AIC    BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)    
fa.config 16 177612 177924 507.76                                  
fa.metric 20 177671 177950 574.83     67.065       4  9.445e-14 ***

What I want to do now is try to free some of the loading and see if I can establish PARTIAL metric invariance. In particular, I want to estimate a version of the metric model where only items 3 and 5 are restricted to have the same loading in both groups. This should amount to a model with 18 degrees of freedom (midway between the two models). Could you please help me get the syntax right for this purpose?

Best,

Giacomo

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: partial metric invariance
parts: I want to estimate a version of the metric model where only items 3 and 5 are restricted to have the same loading in both groups. This should amount to a model with 18 degrees of freedom (midway between the two models). Could you please help me get the syntax right for this purpose?

A model with only 1 loading per factor constrained to equality across groups is statistically equivalent to the configural model.  Imagine you fixed a factor loading instead of factor variances to identify the model, and you use items 3 and 5 as the "marker" variables.  Those loadings would be 1 in both groups (equal) and factor variances would be free in both groups.  That is statistically equivalent to fixing the factor variances to 1 in the first group only and constraining the loadings of 3 and 5 to equality across groups. 

To test partial invariance, you need at least 2 items per factor to be constrained to equality.  If you only constrain 1 item's parameter(s) to equality across groups, it does not matter which item you choose (1 and 4, 1 and 5, 1 and 6, 2 and 4, 2 and 5, ...) -- all of those models will return identical fit.

FYI, there is a function called partial() in the semTools package that you might find useful.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Dear Terrence,

thanks for your answer. I suspected I was getting something substantially wrong!

One more thing if I may: I've been trying to further the analysis to scalar invariance, but I'm struggling to get the syntax right in freeing/constraining the intercept.
In studying partial METRIC invariance, I'm able to use the following syntax to free the loading on X5 across the two groups - coupled with group.equal=c('loadings')
m.fa.metric5 <- ('  
          EXT =~ c(NA,NA)*X1 + c(l2,l2)*X2 + c(l3,l3)*X3
          INT =~ c(NA,NA)*X4 + c(l51,l52)*X5 + c(l6,l6)*X6

EXT ~~ c(1,NA)*EXT
          INT ~~ c(1,NA)*INT
        ')

However when I try to do the same with the intercepts (thresholds, in this case, since I'm working with categorical data), I can't seem to do the same. I want to free the intercept for X5 and fix all the other ones. I first tried the following - coupled with group.equal=c('loadings', 'intercepts'):
m.fa.metric5 <- ('  
          EXT =~ c(NA,NA)*X1 + c(l2,l2)*X2 + c(l3,l3)*X3
          INT =~ c(NA,NA)*X4 + c(l51,l52)*X5 + c(l6,l6)*X6

EXT ~~ c(1,NA)*EXT
          INT ~~ c(1,NA)*INT

X5 ~ c(m51,m52)
        ')
but I get the following error:
Error in lav_syntax_parse_rhs(rhs = rhs.formula[[2L]], op = op) : 
  lavaan ERROR: I'm confused parsing this line: cm51m52

So I tried dropping "intercepts" from group.equal, and fixing the other intercepts across groups manually in the syntax, as follows:
m.fa.scalar5 <- ('  
          EXT =~ c(NA,NA)*X1 + c(l2,l2)*X2 + c(l3,l3)*X3
          INT =~ c(NA,NA)*X4 + c(l51,l52)*X5 + c(l6,l6)*X6

EXT ~~ c(1,NA)*EXT
          INT ~~ c(1,NA)*INT

X1 ~ m1
          X2 ~ m2
          X3 ~ m3
          X4 ~ m4
          X6 ~ m6
        ')

where I get
Error in lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  : 
  lavaan ERROR: some variables have no values (only missings) or no variance
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In is.na(x) : is.na() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'NULL'
2: In is.na(x) : is.na() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'NULL'
3: In is.na(x) : is.na() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'NULL'
4: In is.na(x) : is.na() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'NULL'
5: In is.na(x) : is.na() applied to non-(list or vector) of type 'NULL'

I also tried stuff like X1 ~ c(m1,m1), but this gives me the same parsing error as above.

Could you help me get this right?

Thanks so much!

Giacomo

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: partial metric invariance
parts:
X5 ~ c(m51,m52)

You are providing a label without completing the equation

X5 ~ c(m51, m52)*1

But it makes no sense to constrain intercepts for an item whose loadings are not constrained.

Furthermore, you are only constraining the third item for INT.  Recall my previous post.

If you want to estimate the loadings for the first item per factor, you don't need to use c(NA, NA) in the syntax if you use std.lv = TRUE in the call to cfa().

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
